title: Is USC's Lincoln Riley on the Hot Seat? Mark Followill Weighs In
htmlContent:
USC began the 2026 season with the nation's No. 1 recruiting class, a returning star quarterback and a Hall of Fame defensive coordinator. That combination raised expectations for Lincoln Riley's fifth season in Los Angeles. According to Mark Followill, it also raised the stakes.

Followill is the longtime play-by-play voice of the Dallas Mavericks and also calls college football for the Big Ten Network. He spoke with LandonBuford.com about whether Riley's job could be in jeopardy if the Trojans fall short of the College Football Playoff.

Expectations Have Caught Up With Riley

Riley arrived from Oklahoma in 2021 with a mandate to return USC to the national title conversation. The Trojans have won plenty of games under him, but they have yet to reach the playoff. Last season ended 9-4 after an overtime loss to TCU in the Alamo Bowl. Followill said that history, combined with a top-ranked recruiting class, leaves little room for another near miss.

"Given how highly the recruiting class was rated and what the expectations are, USC obviously has high expectations, and he's done a fine job there. But of course, the expectation is to be in the College Football Playoff. So I don't see how you could say he wouldn't be, whether that's fair or not."

Followill was careful to separate the quality of Riley's work from the pressure that comes with the job. In his view, the modern sport simply doesn't give coaches at elite programs much patience.

"The reality of college football these days is that if you're at a big-time program and you were brought in to help the team take the next step, and you haven't been able to take that next step — and for them, the next step is being a consistent participant in the College Football Playoff — then, unfortunately for him, that would probably be accurate."

Maiava Leads One of the Nation's Best Offenses

If USC does reach the playoff, its offense will likely be the reason. Jayden Maiava led the nation with a 91.2 QBR last season and threw for 3,711 yards. He entered 2026 on several national award watch lists, including the Davey O'Brien Award, which goes to the country's top quarterback.

"We know they have a great offense. Jayden Maiava is, at a minimum, a Davey O'Brien Award candidate. He's one of the best quarterbacks in the country."

Followill pointed to the pieces around Maiava as well. That includes a group of freshman receivers from the top-ranked recruiting class and a backfield that gives Riley two reliable options.

"They need to continue to get great quarterback play, continue to get production from the freshman receivers, and continue to have this one-two punch at running back between Waymond Jordan and King Miller. And then it all boils down to how far USC can make strides on the defensive side of the football. They've got players who are capable. We've seen moments this year, but those moments haven't been consistent enough."

Patterson's Defense Holds the Key

Defense has been the recurring question throughout Riley's tenure, and USC addressed it in January by hiring Gary Patterson as defensive coordinator. Patterson built TCU into a national power over more than two decades with a defense-first approach before stepping away from head coaching in 2021.

Asked who might replace Riley if the season goes south, Followill declined to speculate. Instead, he expressed confidence in the current staff, including a coach he knows well from his years broadcasting in North Texas.

"Out of respect for them, I'm not comfortable getting into candidates or anything like that. I think Lincoln's a great coach, and obviously [Gary Patterson] is somebody we know very well in the Dallas–Fort Worth area. I think they're very poised to keep it on the tracks."

A Signature Win and Some Margin for Error

USC sits at 6-1, and its résumé already includes one of the biggest road wins of the season. On Oct. 10, the Trojans beat Penn State 31-23 at Beaver Stadium in the annual White Out game. Followill acknowledged that the Nittany Lions haven't lived up to their early-season billing, but he said the win still carries weight.

"After a great start, Penn State doesn't seem like quite the team we thought they'd be at the beginning of the year. But you've done something if you've gone into Happy Valley, into Beaver Stadium, and won the Whiteout game. So they're very much in the mix. It's all going to come down to the obvious things: Can they improve defensively, and can they keep getting great production from an offense that has the components to be among the most potent in the nation?"

The lone loss came against Oregon. With a 12-team field and a demanding Big Ten schedule, Followill believes one setback, or even two, won't end USC's playoff hopes.

"They've only tripped up once, in the Oregon game. And the great news for them is that, because of their strength of schedule and the stature of the conference they play in, they do have margin for error. Because of the parity in the game right now, multiple-loss teams from the power conferences like the Big Ten and the SEC are going to make the College Football Playoff. So it's all out in front of them to get the job done, and that's got to be the focus right now."

What Comes Next

For Riley, the path is clear. Keep the offense rolling, get more consistent play from Patterson's defense and close out the second half of the schedule. If USC does that, the hot-seat talk will fade quickly. If it doesn't, Followill's assessment suggests the conversation in Los Angeles will grow louder once the season ends.
excerpt: Mark Followill, the longtime play-by-play voice of the Dallas Mavericks and a Big Ten Network college football broadcaster, told LandonBuford.com that Lincoln Riley's job security at USC is tied directly to whether the Trojans reach the College Football Playoff this season.
